title: Continental could close Gqeberha tyre factory, risking 950 jobs
summary: Continental could close Gqeberha tyre factory, risking 950 jobs TimesLIVE Continental is considering closing its tyre manufacturing plant in Gqeberha, putting about 950 jobs at risk in a province already battling the country’s highest unemployment rate. The German tyre manufacturer announced on Friday that it had begun a formal consultation process under Section 189A of the Labour Relations Act to explore alternatives to discontinuing production at the facility. If no viable alternative is found, operations could end by early 2027. Continental attributed the potential closure to years of underutilised production capacity, intensifying price competition from low-cost imports and increasingly challenging market conditions. The company said extensive turnaround efforts had failed to reverse the decline in capacity utilisation. title: AIDC Eastern Cape seeks urgent talks on Continental tyre plant closure
summary: AIDC Eastern Cape seeks urgent talks on Continental tyre plant closure Engineering News The Automotive Industry Development Centre Eastern Cape (AIDC-EC) says it will invite tyre maker Continental, organised labour, the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (dtic), the Eastern Cape government, Nelson Mandela Bay municipality, the Industrial Development Corporation and key tyre customers to a meeting within the next 14 days to discuss the imminent closure of the Continental tyre plant in Gqeberha, in the Eastern Cape. The State-owned body says it intends to “lead the work…to develop costed alternatives within 60 days for consideration by the parties”.

title: South African stakeholders seek alternatives to Continental tyre plant closure - Tyrepress
summary: South African stakeholders seek alternatives to Continental tyre plant closure Tyrepress The prospect of South Africa losing its second tyre manufacturing plant in little more than a year has prompted calls for measures to safeguard the competitiveness and long-term viability of the country’s tyre and wider automotive manufacturing industries. Efforts to avert the proposed closure of Continental’s tyre plant in Gqeberha are gathering momentum, with the Automotive Industry Development Centre Eastern Cape (AIDC-EC) seeking to bring together stakeholders to develop viable alternatives. South African parliamentarians and the country’s Automobile Association (AA) have meanwhile called for government intervention.
